sophie_customer: Hey team — since the 02/14 deploy our service is seeing tool results assigned to the wrong request. Two tools called in parallel, but outputs are being stitched to the other call's response. correlation_id=0f9c7a3d

elaine_support: Sorry you're hitting this. Can you share a minimal repro and the request IDs? Also any logs with correlation_id.

sophie_customer: Minimal repro below. It's basically two simultaneous function calls via the SDK (one for `search_tool`, one for `summarize_tool`). Happens reliably under ~50ms inter-arrival.

sophie_customer: ```json
{"request_id": "req-42", "correlation_id": "0f9c7a3d", "calls": [
  {"tool": "search_tool", "args": {"q": "error rate"}},
  {"tool": "summarize_tool", "args": {"text": "<long>"}}
]}
```

sophie_customer: Response we got (truncated):

sophie_customer: ```
{"req-42": {"results": [{"tool": "search_tool", "out": "Summary of text..."}, {"tool": "summarize_tool", "out": "Top search hits..."}]}}
```

jamal_engineer: That swapped ordering looks like a correlation/association bug in the fanout code path. Can you confirm whether you used `parallel: true` or if the client sent separate requests?

sophie_customer: We send a single request that fans out to two tools concurrently (internal flag). We relied on tool_result indexing to match.

elaine_support: Thanks. We reproduced locally with your payload and see an intermittent association flip when two tool futures resolve within the same tick (hitting the worker pool). Logging shows the tool_result mapping uses a non-atomic incrementer in the router.

deploy_bot: deploy 2026-02-14T03:12:42Z to infra/runtime (sha abc123) :white_check_mark:

ryan_sre: Noted. This could be a race in the async collector. Assigning to eng-runtime. Jamal, can you take the lead?

jamal_engineer: On it. Initial triage: repro at 8/10 with tight concurrency. Likely root cause: tool_result association key derived from an ephemeral index rather than stable call id. Quick patch: switch to using the original call token (call_id) emitted by the router when allocating futures.

megan_pm: Customer reported higher latency spikes and some billing mismatches because results show up on the wrong request. We need an ETA for a patch and whether to throttle parallel fanout as a temporary workaround.

jamal_engineer: ETA for hotfix (validate+rollback): ~4 hours. Hotfix will atomically tag futures with call_id at allocation. Workaround for customers: set fanout concurrency to 1 or add a small jitter between calls.

elaine_support: Sophie — can you toggle the SDK config to force sequential fanout and confirm whether that eliminates the swapping? If yes, we'll issue the hotfix and coordinate a deployment window.

sophie_customer: Toggled to sequential; issue stopped in 30m test. Thx.

ryan_sre: Creating incident ticket INF-2026-1123. Assigning severity P2 since customer data isn't lost but results mis-assigned (billing/consistency impact).

jamal_engineer: Action items: 1) Hotfix branch -> use stable call_id tagging 2) Add unit test simulating near-simultaneous futures 3) Add logging that includes call_id/correlation_id in tool_result emissions 4) Backfill small migration to re-associate any queued responses (if present).

elaine_support: Also let support know to proactively check for any other customers using high parallel fanout; create a quick query on Flow: `select * from tool_results where resolved_without_call_id limit 100`.

megan_pm: I'll draft the external communication for affected customers and include the sequential workaround + ETA.

sophie_customer: Appreciate the fast turnaround. Please keep us looped on the hotfix window and any rollout postmortem.

jamal_engineer: Will post the patch link once ready and request canary on Dedicated before full rollout.

deploy_bot: scheduled canary deploy 2026-02-14T08:30:00Z -> infra/runtime/hotfix-callid-2026-02-14

elaine_support: Closing thread for now; will update when hotfix is verified in canary. :thumbsup:
